mechanics.body_shape: the prologue saves four registers and reads the one stack argument; the byte span between the receiver's +0x1c and +0x18 is divided by 0x18; the quotient is written to the sink; the span is read and divided a SECOND time and that second quotient bounds a countdown loop; each iteration writes one element's word at +0x00 and hands the address of the element's +0x04 to a second callee; a failed write zeroes the verdict byte and lets the countdown run out rather than aborting.

receiver_displacement.0x1c: read at 0x006a154a and 0x006a1574 -- two independent reads, never written through.

mechanics.division: 0x006a1550..0x006a1568 and again 0x006a157c..0x006a158b: MOV EAX,0x2aaaaaab / IMUL ECX / SAR EDX,0x2 / MOV EAX,EDX / SHR EAX,0x1f / ADD EAX,EDX. That is the signed division of the byte span by 0x18, with an ARITHMETIC shift for the quotient and a LOGICAL shift for the sign mask; the model reproduces the sequence instruction for instruction rather than writing `/`, and the model test sweeps it against C `/ 0x18` over -0x1800..0x1800 plus both int32 extremes.
mechanics.double_evaluation: the span and the division are evaluated twice, once either side of the first stream call. The FIRST quotient is the word written to the sink; the SECOND quotient is the loop bound. Nothing in this body can make them differ -- the only call between them writes to a sink, not to the receiver -- so the model keeps them as two separate evaluations rather than folding them. The model test makes them differ on purpose, by having the first call's observer move the receiver's +0x1c, and asserts the loop follows the second.
mechanics.loop: 0x006a1590 TEST EAX,EAX / 0x006a1592 JLE 0x006a15ed is a SIGNED guard, so a negative quotient skips the loop exactly as a zero quotient does -- and the negative count has already been written to the sink by then. Two induction variables are kept apart, as the machine keeps them apart: EDI is a byte offset stepped by 0x18 (0x006a15e2) while [ESP+0x18] is an independent countdown (0x006a15e5 SUB, 0x006a15ea JNZ). The countdown, not the offset, decides when the loop ends.
mechanics.no_abort_on_failure: 0x006a15a2, 0x006a15c2 and 0x006a15da all jump to 0x006a15e0, which is the block the loop tail falls through to. Once the verdict byte is zero, every later iteration takes the skip path and touches nothing, but the countdown still runs to zero. The model reproduces that: no early exit from the loop.
mechanics.spill_slots: the count word goes to the frame slot that held the saved ECX (entry_ESP-0x4) and the element word to the slot that held the saved ESI (entry_ESP-0x10); Ghidra's local list independently places local_4 at Stack[-0x4]. Both are computed from the live stack pointer at the push sites (LEA ECX,[ESP + 0x14] and LEA ECX,[ESP + 0x18]). The addresses are unobservable from outside -- only the value behind them is -- so the model passes ordinary locals and the test asserts the VALUES, not the addresses.
mechanics.store_before_call: 0x006a156b and 0x006a15b4 both store into the spill slot after the argument pushes and before the CALL, so each callee sees the value through the pointer it was handed. The observers read through that pointer, so a model that passed the address of a word it had not yet filled would be caught.
mechanics.return_word: 0x006a15ef MOV AL,BL puts the verdict byte in AL; nothing else in the body writes EAX on any path after the last call. On the empty and negative paths the verdict byte is the first call's return word; on every other path it is the last write from 0x006a15dc, 0x006a15e0 or the byte captured at 0x006a157a.

return_semantics.ownership: The body performs no reference acquisition or release of its own. It reads two receiver words, reads one word per element, and returns a verdict. No record establishes whether the payload address handed to 0x00693390 is borrowed or owned, and none is claimed.

mutation_check.method: each mutation applied to a copy in /tmp, compiled with the same gate and run; the unmutated tree is 131/131 PASS
mutation_check.killed_detail: folding the two quotient evaluations into one (4 checks); stride 0x18 -> 0x4 (12); payload address +0x4 -> +0x0 (7); the count write's third argument 1 -> 0 (7); the signed JLE guard made unsigned (2); SAR EDX,0x2 replaced by a logical shift (15); the element word read from +0x04 instead of +0x00 (9); the count write's verdict ignored (3); the span's sign flipped, end-begin -> begin-end (82); the payload call's third argument 0 -> 1 (3); returning the count call's verdict instead of the accumulated byte (19); the receiver's +0x18 hoisted out of the loop and cached, which the per-use re-read case kills (7).
mutation_check.survived_detail: Two mutations survive, and both survive for a provable reason rather than because the test is blind. (1) Changing the loop tail from `while (--remaining != 0)` to `while (--remaining != 0 && ok)`, i.e. aborting the loop as soon as a write fails instead of counting it out. Once the verdict byte is zero every remaining iteration is `TEST BL,BL / JZ / XOR BL,BL / ADD EDI / SUB / JNZ` -- no transfer, no store to the receiver, no effect on the return word. Aborting and counting out therefore produce the same return word and the same recorded transfer sequence, and no black-box observation over (return value, transfer sequence) can separate them. (2) Deleting the `ok = false` in the skip branch, i.e. dropping the `XOR BL,BL` at 0x006a15e0. All three jumps that reach 0x006a15e0 arrive with BL already zero, so that XOR is a no-op on every reachable path and removing the assignment changes nothing. Both mutations contradict the listing's instruction sequence while preserving its behaviour; the model follows the listing anyway, and the honest statement is that this test cannot refute a behaviour-preserving mutation of the instruction sequence.
